Following Counterpoint Research's earlier report showing Apple's strongest-ever second-quarter iPhone shipments, Omdia has released its own data, also pointing to this record-breaking performance. Details are as follows.

Omdia warns the decline will further intensify

Earlier this morning, we reported on Counterpoint Research's report, which showed preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for the second quarter of 2026.

Counterpoint noted in its report that Samsung led the market with a 24% shipment share, up from 20% a year earlier. Apple followed closely at 20%, also up from 17% last year; Xiaomi fell from 14% to 12%, OPPO from 12% to 11%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Now, Omdia's preliminary report (cited by MacMagazine) points to the same overall trend, though with slightly different estimates.

Omdia puts Samsung's market share at 22%, up from 20% in the second quarter of 2025; Apple is at 20%, up from 16% last year. Xiaomi dropped from 15% to 11%, OPPO from 12% to 10%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Below is Omdia's take on Apple's performance for the quarter:

Omdia says that, unsurprisingly, the ongoing memory crisis has caused overall shipments to fall 4% year-on-year, making the second quarter of 2026 the weakest quarter since the second quarter of 2023.
